name: Low-to-high cable fly
cue: Soft elbows, sweep up and together to chin height.
research: Standing low-to-high cable fly between two low pulleys (0.075 H, 13 cm, on carriages in two columns 0.45 H, 0.8 m, either side of the stance and 0.1 H behind it, the wheels on a fork 0.08 H toward the lifter), the cable crossover stance: staggered (left foot 0.18 H forward, both soles flat), trunk leaned 10 deg with the hinge at the hips (pelvis 8, lumbar 1, thorax 1), knees soft (front 15, back 0). Design values from the standard technique description, not a measured trial: the arms start low and wide at the sides of the hips with a soft elbow (shoulder elevation 36, plane -1 in the frontal plane, elbow 14, hands 0.53 H high and 0.34 H out, shoulder blades retracted: clavicle pro -8) and sweep up and together in a wide arc to chin height in front of the face (elevation 99, plane 102 across the shoulder line, elbow 19, hands 0.89 H high, 0.05 H either side of the midline and 0.38 H ahead, shoulder blades protracted: clavicle pro +8), the elbow keeping its soft bend. Stirrup handles ride on the fists (a free-swinging triangle on the grip bar that follows the cable, dswing; the bar is kept square to the cable). The cables rise from the columns beside and behind the lifter and clear the thighs and trunk (closest 0.03 H, the ring beside the forearm at the top). Cable 1:1 to the stack, 0.52 H of travel. Geometry: design/cableA/lh.mjs.

targets.note: design values (standard technique), not a measured trial; the plane read-back is thorax-relative, the 10 deg forward lean is in the trunk

camera.note: Front three-quarter view, almost level (az 25, el 4, 25 deg off the front view): as the hands finish at chin height the forearms stay above the chest, so the upper chest keeps facing the camera under them, the front shoulders glow beside it, and the towers stand behind the figure.
